summary: Active sense 1 is intentionally broad: physical tightening, binding, powerful throwing/blows, reflexive girding, reliance and social pressure already occur. Noun-specific contexts do not warrant a series of technical or figurative senses.

Count audit: active Infectum has four unnumbered plus three numbered examples, seven sense-1 items total. Most reader thin-cell proposals here are therefore unnecessary. Added only a contracted suffixed form as unusual-form evidence.

Detransitive D1 retains its existing number and intensification meaning, with physical tautness added. D2 introduces general fastening. The two inherited Part. Pass. examples are moved by meaning, not by renumbering existing senses. Bound manuscripts are not sufficient to lexicalize a separate craft sense.

Active Infectum-wa is genuinely absent and now attested with a roller subject, rope fastening, and habitual donkey-load binding. The inherited combined Detransitive heading already contains its own Infectum-wa and cannot be used to infer active coverage.

Valency: tightened body part or binding rope may be direct object; b-/ʕal- mark support/contact or instrument. Social pressure retains ʕal-targets. In 8/16 li hawa has L-agent-style indexing despite intransitive intensification, unlike Detransitive fever ḥiṣo with ʕal-experiencer.

Twelve supplied occurrence records lack verse text/translation. They receive rejected_analysis decisions: the token metadata is retained, but cannot be checked against a source verse. No examples are created from them.
No new Idiomatic phrases: reliance and forceful-blow expressions are already treated under existing sense 1; searches and the supplied entry confirm their existing treatment.

Round 1 already established active Infectum-wa with three examples. Jan ḥayṣiwa therefore supports that box and adds a fourth sense-1 context, not a new box. Parallel maḥtiwa and repetition kul naqqa identify a habitual sequence; the cover material is supplied by mede ḥreno in the preceding clause.

Both Jan tokens are active I. No new Detransitive sense or morphology follows from these data. The transitive patient ḥaṣe is explicit in the first; the second uses ʕal for the contact surface, with the material understood. Source English is project machine translation and the claim that it had become wine is not used to identify the verb’s lexical meaning.
Supply source verses for the records marked rejected_analysis; morphology and sense remain provisional there.

Resolve Prym–Socin concordance: supplied PrS 3/6 versus inherited prs 8/34 for the government clause; PrS 17/32 versus inherited prs 40/3 for the bound girl. These cannot safely be changed without the edition's numbering key.
Confirm ḥayṣe- Imperativ (58/53), ḥṣila (107/25), ḥəṣile (PrS 8/6), s/ṣ and h/ḥ spellings, and ḥoṣṣe (67/20). No silent normalization.
MAC Ishaq Material culture/108: is ḥiso with šuġlo an adjective 'hard/strenuous' of this root, and is final ḥiṣo a bag property or manner modifier? Both remain unquoted pending classification.
Talay 2/12: does ḥiṣiwa specifically denote bookbinding or compact manufacture? Retain general fastening only.
Confirm 8/16 li hawa syntax and PrS 3/6 Ḥiṣo agreement. At 70/162 aʕle follows feminine mare; check reference and gender.

Jan 2.4/584: does ḥəṣle ḥaṣe describe support/bracing for a bodily complaint, or tightening the cloth around the back? Both fit inherited I.1; the immediate Turoyo does not justify a narrower medical or garment sense.

summary: Moral solidarity, reliance with ḥaṣo b-, animal reflexive constriction, inanimate roller as agent, and hard work as a property bearer extend existing strength/tightening. Reliance is already illustrated in the first Infectum section; no duplicate idiom added.

Back bracing with direct ḥaṣe and pressure used to reseal container mouths with ʕal femayye both continue the broad physical tightening/pressing sense. Neither requires a technical sealing sense or a new Idiomatic phrase.
